newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary BUX index hits record at 4,134.31, up 9.50.
newsitem.headline: Hungary BUX index hits record at 4,134.31, up 9.50.

text.p: The Budapest Stock Exchange's (BSE) BUX index hit its tenth record high in a row, closing the year in an upbeat mood with dealers seeing no obvious reasons for a correction to follow.
"I do not expect a dramatic crumble, but it would be difficult to give precise forecasts as the next day of trade is January 6," said Balazs Bathory of Creditanstalt Securities.

Oil and gas company MOL and chemicals companies Borsodchem and TVK accounted for more than half of the spot share turnover, with MOL putting on 15 to close at 2,020 forints, TVK ending at 1,840, up 30, and Borsodchem finishing 50 forints higher at 4,050.
The BUX closed the year at 4,134.31 points, up 9.50 points or 0.23 percent.
Nine shares hit new highs but Bathory said there was no obvious reason.
"Most shares have been rising for some days and were bound to reach record levels," he said. "There is no logic for hitting new records today but it certainly has a psychological effect".
He added that the Budapest Stock Exchange's performance surpassed expectations this month.
"The bourse has this month produced the gains most people only expected to be achieved during January and February," Bathori said.
During 1996 the BUX index rose 170 percent to 4,134.31 points from 1,528.92, second only to Venezuela with returns in dollar terms of more than 98.3 percent over the year.
BUX index futures also expressed optimism by rising 12 to 70 points, with March 1997 ending at 4,277 points, up 17 and June 1998 at 5,085 points, up 70.
